key_insight: GutCore is a foundation model that can analyze an entire endoscopy case, not just single frames, to assess gastric cancer presence, invasion depth, biomarkers, and prognosis.
clinical_relevance: This could help make endoscopic assessment more patient-level and comprehensive, potentially supporting earlier risk stratification and treatment planning in gastric cancer.
method: Pretrained on 5.6 million de-identified endoscopic images from 10+ hospitals.
Evaluated on open image-level datasets and an internal cohort of 11,035 endoscopic examinations.
Aggregated all images from each exam for patient-level predictions of cancer status, invasion depth, biomarkers, and survival.
evidence_signal: In the internal cohort, GutCore achieved AUCs of 0.995 for cancer detection, 0.960 for muscularis propria invasion, and 0.804 for SM2-or-deeper invasion, with strong survival stratification in advanced gastric cancer.
watch_item: The model needs validation in independent clinical cohorts before routine use, and performance was lower for some biomarkers such as HER2.
paper_title: GutCore: An Endoscopy Foundation Model for Whole-Case Gastric Cancer Analysis
